entities.summary:
Joaquín Setantí y Alcina (unknown–1617) was a prominent figure in the intellectual landscape of early modern Barcelona, Spain. 







 Setantí's most notable contributions to the movement of tacitism, a philosophical approach emphasizing the importance of moral aphorisms, include his 1590 publication, Frutos de historia, and the 1614 collection, Centellas de varios conceptos. This latter work, comprising 500 dense aphorisms, showcases Setantí's originality and foreshadows the development of aphorisms by Baltasar Gracián and other prominent figures of the Spanish Baroque. 







 Setantí's legacy as a precursor to the aphorism movement has endured, influencing the development of Spanish literature and philosophy during this period. His work continues to be studied by scholars today, offering insights into the intellectual currents of early modern Europe.


 Joaquín Setantí y Alcina's impact on the intellectual world of his time is a testament to the enduring power of his ideas.

entities.summary:
Joaquín Setantí y Alcina (1550-1617) was a pivotal figure in the intellectual landscape of Barcelona during the early seventeenth century.




He played a pivotal role in the tacitist movement, which sought to revive classical Roman ethics through the use of aphorisms. His most notable work, Centellas de varios conceptos (1614), is a seminal collection of moral aphorisms that showcased his unique contribution to the genre.




Setantí's work had a lasting impact on the development of Spanish Baroque literature, influencing writers such as Baltasar Gracián and fostering a new era of aphoristic writing.





A remarkable example of the power of intellectual exchange, Setantí's Centellas continue to inspire scholars and writers to this day.
